content.user_title: Design Agent Tools That Models Use Reliably
content.value_statement: Agent tools fail when descriptions, schemas, and error messages are ambiguous. This skill gives practical patterns for clearer tool APIs, safer consolidation, and better testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains how tool descriptions act as prompts for agent behavior.
Provides criteria for clear parameters, returns, errors, and examples.
Shows when to consolidate overlapping tools into broader workflows.
Describes MCP tool namespacing and fully qualified tool names.
Includes Python templates for description, schema, and error message generation.
Offers evaluation criteria for clarity, completeness, recoverability, efficiency, and consistency.
limitations: It gives design guidance, not a complete production tool framework.
The command execution examples require strict sandboxing before real deployment.
It does not validate a live MCP server or generated schema automatically.
Some case study references are illustrative and should be verified before strategic decisions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Tool APIs
use_cases.description: Define naming, parameter, and response conventions for a shared tool catalog.

use_cases.title: Reduce Tool Selection Confusion
use_cases.description: Identify overlapping tools and consolidate workflows that cause selection errors.

use_cases.title: Improve Tool Failure Recovery
use_cases.description: Rewrite errors so agents know what failed and how to retry.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Tool Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single tool.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tool description for clarity, missing inputs, returns, and error guidance. Suggest concise improvements: [paste tool description].

prompt_templates.title: Create A Tool Contract
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a new tool from a workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool contract for this workflow. Include name, when to use it, parameters, return shape, and recoverable errors: [describe workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate A Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these tools for overlap and selection ambiguity. Recommend which tools to merge, keep separate, or namespace: [paste tool list].

prompt_templates.title: Design And Test A Tool System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a production agent system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a tool design plan for this agent system. Include tool boundaries, MCP naming, response formats, error recovery, test cases, and deployment risks: [describe system].

output_examples.input: A support agent has separate tools for finding customers, listing orders, and issuing refunds.
output: Combine customer and order lookup when they serve one support workflow.
Keep refund authorization separate because it changes account state.
Document the handoff from lookup results to refund review.

output_examples.input: A database lookup tool returns large records and generic errors.
output: Add concise and detailed response modes for different task needs.
Replace generic failures with specific causes and retry guidance.
Include examples of valid identifiers and expected results.

output_examples.input: An MCP integration has ambiguous tool names across servers.
output: Use server-scoped names in prompts and documentation.
Group related tools under clear namespaces.
Add examples that show the intended tool for each workflow.

best_practices: Document what the tool does, when to use it, expected inputs, returned data, and recoverable errors.
Consolidate tools only when they support one clear workflow and do not hide important safety boundaries.
Test descriptions with representative agent requests and revise based on observed failure modes.
anti_patterns: Using vague names or descriptions that force the agent to guess the tool purpose.
Merging unrelated tools only to reduce tool count.
Returning verbose data by default when a concise format would answer the task.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, platform teams, and AI product teams who design tools for agents can use it.

faq.question: Does it build tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and sample helper patterns that a developer can adapt.

faq.question: Does it support MCP tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains namespacing and fully qualified tool names for Model Context Protocol integrations.

faq.question: Can it reduce tool sprawl?
faq.answer: Yes. It offers consolidation criteria for overlapping tools and workflows.

faq.question: What should I watch for in production?
faq.answer: Treat command execution and file access patterns as privileged capabilities that need sandboxing, logging, and policy controls.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is general guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
